full_judgment: 2. The pre-emptor filed the case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 alleging, inter alia, that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance as well as by purchase in the case jote through Kabala deed dated 11.05.1987. The case land belonged to the respondent opposite party No. 2 Lolit Chandra Roy, who sold the same to the pre-emptee respondent no. 1 by registered sale deed dated 21.01.1988 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor petitioner. The respondent no. 2 also did not serve any notice of transfer upon the pre-emptee, and the other co-sharers of the case jote. The pre-emptee is a Stanger to the case jote. The pre-emptor has about 4/5 bighas of land, who getting knowledge about the aforesaid sale of the case land dated 21.14.1998 from local people instituted this case within time for pre-emption of the case land on depositing the statutory amount of money. The pre-emptor being a co-sharer in the case jote is entitled to get the case land by way of pre-emption.
